text: Barley failed across much of the Tavrin Valley this season after a stretch of late frost, dry winds and patchy irrigation left heads thin and fields undersized, according to local officials and growers. The valley’s agricultural bureau said Monday that only about 38% of expected barley was harvested from the main basin, with losses heaviest near South Kellan and Merrow Ford. Some farmers have already ploughed under stunted plots to prepare for autumn rye. “This was a hard season for barley, and the yield shortfall is worse than we first projected,” said Nira Pell, deputy director of the Tavrin Valley Crop Office. Wheat and beet plantings held up better, but feed prices are expected to rise in the district.
